name: The Week Ender
blurb: A plan for the weekend, made before the weekend starts. Three questions, one plan.
story: I built this because I know what happens on Friday.
You've worked all week. You're tired. The weekend starts, and suddenly all the good intentions go out the window.
The Week Ender gives you a plan before the weekend starts.
Three questions. A simple plan. Something to follow when Friday turns into Saturday and Saturday turns into *“I'll start again Monday.”*
**I needed this. So I built it.**

name: Cabin Notes
blurb: Everything about a seasonal cabin in one place — and it still works with no signal.
story: I own a seasonal cabin.
And every time we went up there, somebody forgot something.
Or we couldn't remember what was already there.
Or something needed fixing.
Or somebody asked, *“How do you turn the water on again?”*
So I built the app I wanted to have.
Keep track of what's at the cabin. Take pictures. Make the bring-list. Keep the opening and closing checklist. Send guests the instructions.
And when you're sitting at the cabin with no cell service?
**It still works.**

name: Footsteps of the Teacher
blurb: Kids learn real code by building Bible stories, with an owl who helps instead of scolding.
story: I wanted my kids to learn how to code.
But I didn't want them staring at another boring programming tutorial.
I wanted them to build something they already knew.
**Bible stories.**
So I started building a world where kids learn real code by making those stories come alive.
Write the code. See what happens.
Make the donkey move. Build the story. Fix the mistake.
And when the code doesn't work, Ada the owl is there to help instead of making them feel stupid.
**Kids don't need another game that wastes their time. They need something that makes them want to learn.**

name: Strongman Contest
blurb: Run a whole contest from one phone, in a basement, with no internet.
story: I've run strongman contests.
I've stood in a gym trying to keep track of points, placings, ties, and events while also trying to actually run the contest.
And a lot of the time you're in a basement with **zero cell service.**
So I built the scoring system I wanted.
One phone.
No internet.
Enter the athletes. Enter the events. Let the app do the math.
The scoring works the way a strongman contest should work.
**I didn't build this because I thought there was a huge market for strongman scoring apps.**
I built it because **I run strongman contests.**

name: Season Book
blurb: A gymnast's whole season, kept on your own iCloud and turned into a scrapbook you can send.
story: If you're a gymnastics parent, you know the feeling.
Your kid competes all season. Meet after meet, score after score.
But Grandma and Grandpa can't always make it.
Mom might be at one kid's meet while Dad is taking another kid somewhere else.
Sometimes the people who want to be there the most simply can't be.
So I built Season Book.
Keep the whole season in one place. Scores, personal bests, memories — all of it.
Then turn the season into a scrapbook you can send to Grandma and Grandpa, or sit down at home and watch it together on the TV.
Because the season shouldn't only belong to the people who were sitting in the bleachers.
And your memories shouldn't belong to somebody else's server.
**Your data. Your memories. You own them. Always.**

name: Two or Three
blurb: Named for the verse in Matthew. Two or three people, one topic, ten minutes of actually talking.
story: The name comes from one of my favorite verses in the Bible. Matthew 18:20.
> *“Where two or three are gathered, I will be there.”* — Jesus
I wanted that for my kids. I wanted it for my family. And then I figured other families could probably use it too.
This one started with something I kept thinking about:
**What if we actually put our phones down and talked to each other?**
Two or three people around a table.
One topic.
Everybody gets a question that makes sense for where they are in life.
A six-year-old shouldn't get the same question as a fourteen-year-old.
You talk.
You listen.
Ten minutes later, the phone goes face down.
That's it.
No ads. No subscription. Nothing to buy.
Just people talking.
**Because I think we need more of that.**

name: Spotter
blurb: The gym CRM for the person who owns the gym and still unlocks the door in the morning.
story: I own a gym.
I know what it's like to be the person doing everything.
Training people. Scheduling people. Keeping track of sessions. Collecting payments. Trying to remember who trained when.
And then doing it all again tomorrow.
Spotter is the gym CRM I wanted.
**Not for a corporation with 500 employees.**
For the person who owns the gym and is still the one unlocking the door in the morning.
Clients. Sessions. Payments. Simple.
Your data stays yours. No server. No monthly fee.
**Just the stuff you actually need.**

name: BizLedger
blurb: What came in, what went out, how many miles — without becoming an accountant.
story: I have friends who own businesses who don't need QuickBooks.
They don't need a financial department.
They don't need a 47-step reconciliation process.
They just need to know:
**What came in?** **What went out?** **How many miles did I drive?**
That's BizLedger.
I built it for the person who has a business but doesn't want their bookkeeping app to become another job.
Simple accounting. No bank connection. No complicated chart of accounts.
**No nonsense.**

name: Polly
blurb: Every voice deserves to be remembered.
story: Polly started with a simple question:
**“Where did I put that?”**
And then I started thinking about something bigger.
Every family has knowledge that exists nowhere except inside somebody's head.
Where things are. How things work. The stories. The memories.
The little things that somebody knows because they've been around long enough to know them.
What happens when that person isn't there anymore?
So Polly became more than a voice assistant.
It's about remembering.
**Every voice deserves to be remembered.**

name: Workout Tracker
blurb: I write the program, you open your phone and do the work. $20 a month, first week free.
story: This is probably the most obvious one.
**I'm a coach. I needed a workout tracker.**
I didn't want another complicated fitness app trying to be your coach.
I wanted something where **I** could write the program and my clients could simply open their phone and do the work.
Set by set. Workout by workout. Keep going.

There are over 1,400 exercise videos in it, with the variations, so you can see the movement before you do it. Travel workouts for when you're away from your gym. And a mobility library for when something is bothering you.
This is the one I use with the people I train.
Start with the basic app — **$20 a month.** The first week is free and it doesn't ask for a card, so you can see whether you like it before you pay for anything.
Fill in the notes when you start. That is how I get to know you and what you're actually after.
**Then I can help guide you on your journey.**
